headline: The overnight rebound held and broadened in Europe, helped by Beijing's market pledge, while French data point to softer inflation and a shrinking economy

findings.headline: Beijing puts the state behind its stock market
findings.body: A State Council meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang called for a bigger role for 'national team' investors, with Central Huijin acting as a quasi-stabilisation fund to keep liquidity ample, plus incentives for dividends, buybacks and long-term investors. Mainland shares had their biggest day since the October 2024 stimulus, led by chips, and the STAR 50 tech index jumped 15%. It gives the global tech rebound a policy backstop in Asia, though analysts note a lasting recovery still needs better earnings and domestic demand.

sources.label: CNA/Reuters: China stocks surge most in two years as Beijing vows stronger market support
CNBC: China's chip stocks log biggest one-day gain

findings.headline: France: Q3 GDP revised to a contraction and inflation drops sharply
findings.body: INSEE revised French third-quarter GDP to -0.2% from a first estimate of -0.1%, after a flat second quarter. Provisional November CPI slowed to 2.9% y/y from 3.4% (HICP 3.2% from 3.7%) as petroleum product prices cooled and services eased, with prices down 0.7% on the month. A weak economy with falling inflation strengthens the case for the ECB to lean dovish, ahead of German flash CPI on Monday and the euro-area flash next week.

findings.headline: Precious and industrial metals bounce as the AI scare fades
findings.body: Gold is coming back from its lowest level in about a year, silver is outpacing it, and copper is joining in. Commentary links the move to easing AI jitters: the tech rout had forced selling of metals for cash, and that pressure is lifting. Higher Fed-rate expectations and a firm dollar remain the headwind, so the bounce looks like a reversal of forced selling rather than a new trend so far.

sources.label: CNBC: Gold rebounds from one-year low as AI jitters ease
Investing.com: Gold jumps after hitting 15-month low earlier this week

view: Our view: The overnight story held and got bigger. Beijing's backstop and fading AI fears are driving a broad risk-on morning, with chips, Asia and metals leading. France's soft data add a dovish tilt for the ECB. The thin US half-day (closing 19:00 Zurich) and Sunday's OPEC+ meeting are the next tests of whether this is more than a relief rally.

regions.label: Europe
regions.text: Broad gains through the morning, with tech and miners leading on the China support pledge and the metals bounce; Imperial Brands is re-rated on Altria's possible cash bid.

regions.label: Asia
regions.text: China's State Council pledge drove the mainland's best day since October 2024, with chips and Hong Kong tech leading; Seoul extended the chip rebound.

regions.label: US
regions.text: Futures carry the rebound into a half-day post-Thanksgiving session that closes 19:00 Zurich, so liquidity is thin.

assets.label: Metals
assets.text: Gold, silver and copper rebound as forced selling from the tech rout eases; Fed-hike pricing and a firm dollar are the headwind.

assets.label: Oil
assets.text: Crude keeps its Gulf risk premium ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting on January quotas and the disputed capacity audit.
